text:
Maya: FYI, new reranker v2-quant results are weird — offline eval (sample_v2) shows +0.9 NDCG but the shadow A/B on staging shows -1.8 MRR. opening a triage thread.
Alex: ugh, that gap sounds large. did we change the candidate ordering or dedupe logic between eval and shadow?
Maya: no change in reranker code. differences I can see: (1) eval uses sampled top-50 candidates, shadow uses top-100 with reservoir dedupe; (2) we ran quant PTQ-int8 with per-channel scaling; (3) inference batched at 8 in shadow to hit throughput.
Priya: batching could change KV cache timings for long queries — have we replicated exact seq lengths?
Maya: quick sanity: eval median seq_len=64, shadow median=78. also tokenization: eval used our offline tokenizer (v1.2) while shadow uses runtime tokenizer v1.3 (minor casing tweak).
Jonah: can you paste the metric snapshot?
Maya: ```
# offline eval (sample_v2)
model: rerank-v2-quant
ndcg@10: 0.412 (+0.009 vs baseline)
mrr@10: 0.288 (+0.002)
# shadow (staging) - 24h
ndcg@10: 0.405 (+0.004)
mrr@10: 0.264 (-0.018)
```
Alex: MRR drop is concentrated in short queries? slice by query_len?
Maya: yes — short queries (<16 tokens) MRR down -0.05, long queries neutral/positive.
Priya: that screams priming/primed-candidate-order effects. with batching=8 maybe candidates are being concatenated differently? any evidence of token truncation?
Maya: logs show a handful of "kvcache-miss" warnings when batchsize>1 for short queries. also saw a note in runtime: "pack_candidates=True" does different padding in batched mode.
Jonah: that could alter context length per candidate -> reranker sees more/less context and ranking flips.
Alex: for quant angle: did you test int8 vs fp16 for the short-query slice? small perturbations could flip top-1 and hit MRR a lot.
Maya: only large-sweep was int8 on sample_v2. I queued a quick compare; will run `eval_harness --model rerank-v2 --quant int8,int4,fp16 --slice short_queries --batch 1,8` on a small holdout.
Priya: also try running with tokenizer v1.2 vs v1.3 to isolate tokenization delta.
Maya: noted. earliest runs:
```
# quick-run results (small holdout)
rerank-v2 fp16 batch=1 tokenizer=v1.2 mrr@10: 0.291
rerank-v2 int8  batch=1 tokenizer=v1.2 mrr@10: 0.288
rerank-v2 int8  batch=8 tokenizer=v1.2 mrr@10: 0.286
rerank-v2 int8  batch=8 tokenizer=v1.3 mrr@10: 0.271
```
Jonah: whoa tokenizer change plus batching moved mrr way down. that's a strong signal.
Alex: action plan: (A) repro matrix: batch 1 vs 8, tokenizer v1.2 vs v1.3, quant int8 vs fp16 on same candidate pool; (B) instrument ranker inputs in shadow to log tokenized lengths and kvcache events for short queries; (C) run a small canary in prod with batch=1 int8 to validate.
Priya: while we're at it, confirm candidate normalization (url/case) parity between offline and production preproc. those normalize steps have caused anchor flips before.
Maya: added candidate-normalization check to the matrix.
ci-bot: scheduled job `rerank/trisage/1765436789` -> running 12 runs (expected ~45m). i'll post results when done.
Maya: thanks — I'll own the triage. tagging @alex @priya for follow-ups.
Alex: ping if you want help parsing the diffs, I can diff tokenization outputs.
Priya: I'll add a unit test in the eval harness to ensure tokenizer parity and a short-query MRR smoke.
Maya: current owner notes: repro in 2 hours, if it's tokenizer+batching we'll roll batch->1 for short queries and run canary. will update thread with final numbers. :thumbsup:
Jonah: FYI, if we end up rolling batch->1, please file an infra request for throughput impact so SRE can advise autoscale.
Maya: will do. thanks everyone.
